learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Encephalopathy Patterns.
Apply Encephalopathy Patterns to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Triphasic morphology, periodic discharges, diffuse slowing and altered reactivity can occur in toxic-metabolic, infectious, hypoxic or structural conditions.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: These patterns are often nonspecific and exist on an ictal–interictal continuum. Interpretation requires clinical, laboratory and imaging context.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: EEG can detect severity and trajectory when behavioural examination is limited.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Attributing a pattern to one disease without corroboration can misdirect care.

reviewPrompts.answer: These patterns are often nonspecific and exist on an ictal–interictal continuum. Interpretation requires clinical, laboratory and imaging context.
EEG can detect severity and trajectory when behavioural examination is limited.
Attributing a pattern to one disease without corroboration can misdirect care.
Use EEG to describe physiology precisely, then integrate cause cautiously.
